query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Controlled annealing of FeNiCrCoCu HEA coatings promotes the in situ formation of a continuous, Cu-rich oxide layer that acts as a protective barrier during high-temperature sliding, thereby reducing wear rates and altering the microscopic deformation behavior from severe plastic/adhesive deformation toward a more benign, oxide-governed regime.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate with no preformed oxide layer.
generation.intervention: Applying a controlled annealing treatment (e.g., at ≈300°C) designed to encourage oxidation of the Cu component within the alloy.
generation.conditions: High-temperature sliding wear regime (operating temperature around 300°C or higher) under comparable loads and sliding speeds to standard baseline tests.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous, Cu-rich oxide (such as CuO) film on the coating surface.
generation.mechanism: The protective Cu-rich oxide film reduces direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding, thereby shifting the deformation mechanism from adhesive/plastic damage of the metallic coating to less severe abrasive or oxidative wear. This transition mitigates severe microscopic plastic deformation and intergranular fracture by buffering and redistributing tribological stresses.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-deposited baseline, the annealed coating will exhibit a lower wear rate, a reduced coefficient of friction, and microstructural evidence of milder, oxide-mediated deformation instead of pronounced plastic deformation or intergranular fracture under high-temperature sliding conditions.
generation.baseline: The as-deposited HEA coating without post-deposition annealing and with minimal native oxidation.
generation.boundary: The predicted benefits are expected to hold in the high-temperature regime (around 300°C and above) where oxidation is sufficient to form the protective film; at lower temperatures the oxide layer may not develop adequately and the wear resistance improvements would likely not manifest.
generation.uncertainty: The exact annealing temperature and duration needed for optimal Cu-oxide formation, its uniformity, and long-term stability under cyclic sliding conditions remain to be fully determined. Additionally, possible interactions or segregation effects involving the other alloying elements (Fe, Ni, Cr, Co) may influence the oxide film's protective efficacy.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of FeNiCrCoCu HEA-coated metal substrates. One set will undergo controlled annealing at approximately 300°C to promote Cu oxidation, while the other set will remain in the as-deposited state. Both sets will then be subjected to standardized sliding wear tests at high temperature (≈300°C) under identical loads and sliding speeds. Comparative analysis will be performed on wear rate, coefficient of friction, and microstructural deformation (using SEM/TEM and surface composition analysis such as XPS or EDS).
measurements: Surface oxide layer characterization (thickness and composition)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed samples do not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in wear rate and alteration in deformation behavior (with evidence of a continuous, protective Cu-rich oxide film) compared to the as-deposited samples, or if the oxide layer forms non-uniformly or degrades rapidly during sliding, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

System: AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 high-entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Inert gas atomisation using argon followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1050 °C for 10 min under 50 MPa compaction pressure, with passive cooling at 150 K/min until 300 °C.
